label: D-Link DGS-1210-10P
description: D-Link DGS-1210-10P (Rev F) smart managed PoE switch: 8x 10/100/1000BASE-T PoE+ RJ-45 on a 65 W budget, 2x 100/1000 Mbps SFP cages, 20 Gbps, 14.88 Mpps, fanless, external 54 V DC adapter.

fabric.note: 20 Gbps switching capacity and 14.88 Mpps maximum 64-byte forwarding rate for the DGS-1210-10P, from the DGS-1210 Series Rev F datasheet specification table (https://www.dlink.com/us/en/-/media/business_products/dgs/dgs-1210/datasheet/dgs1210seriesrevfdatasheet211enus.pdf). 10 ports x 2 Gbps full duplex, so an RJ45/SFP combo pair counts once whichever medium is in use.

notes: Ports, per the DGS-1210 Series Rev F datasheet (hardware Rev. F, 2.11 EN US, 05-SEP-2018): 8 x 10/100/1000BASE-T PoE (802.3af/at) on ports 1-8 plus 2 x 100/1000 Mbps SFP cages. 8K MAC entries, 256 static MAC entries, 4.1 Mbits packet buffer, DDR3 128 MB CPU memory, 32 MB flash, 256 static VLAN groups (VID 1-4094), 802.1D/802.1w/802.1s STP, 802.3ad LACP (8 groups of up to 8 ports), jumbo frames to 10,000 bytes, and 124 IPv4 / 50 IPv6 static routes over 4 IP interfaces - static routing, not a routing protocol, which is what puts this in the L3-lite class. Management is web GUI, compact CLI over Telnet, SNMP v1/v2c/v3 and D-Link Network Assistant; no model in the line has a serial console port (the console row in the datasheet is an LED, not a port). Dual software images and dual configuration files. Fanless (0 dB(A), Fans: No), 280 x 126 x 44 mm, 0.95 kg, 81.9 W at 100 V with PoE enabled, 2.03 W standby. The only model in the Rev F line powered by an external 54.0 V DC power adapter rather than an internal supply, which is why its maximum draw is quoted per mains voltage. Time-based PoE scheduling is supported. Source: https://www.dlink.com/us/en/-/media/business_products/dgs/dgs-1210/datasheet/dgs1210seriesrevfdatasheet211enus.pdf

poe.note: 65 W PoE power budget for ports 1-8, all 802.3af/802.3at capable, from the Rev F specification table and ordering information. An earlier revision of the same series datasheet (Rev C) prints 78 W for the DGS-1210-10P, so the two revisions disagree by 13 W and the current Rev F figure is recorded. 8 x 30 W of 802.3at cannot be delivered at once: 65 W is 4 ports at 30 W or 4 at 15.4 W, so the budget binds, not the port.
